rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-3 report the authors' own case study (Senyera WUA, Valencia), a hydraulic model calibrated with five pressure sensors (Section 2.2), GA optimisation runs for 12 sectoring scenarios (Table 6) and energy indicators compared with 2006 billing data (Tables 8-9).
rows.notes: The study reports no result of its own on water applied versus crop water requirement or on water-management inefficiency from fixed irrigation times. All scenarios use a fixed 2 h period per sector (Section 2.4) and the only outputs are pump pressure settings, energy consumption and cost (Tables 4-9); predicted energy savings of up to 36.4% (scenario 2). Water volumes at intakes are used only to check the model water balance (+1.3%). The passage's claim about unequal water delivery is the citing review's own inference, not a finding of this study.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-3 report the authors' own case study, calibrated EPANET/HuraGIS model (relative pressure error +2.8%, Section 2.2), GA scenario runs (Table 6) and comparison with 2006 energy data (Tables 8-9).
rows.notes: The study does not evaluate whether crop water requirements are satisfied, nor any flexibility of intake operation outside fixed periods; its methodology explicitly groups intakes into sectors operating in fixed 2 h scheduled periods and optimises only energy consumption (WPD) and cost. The improvement described in the passage (intakes operating within rather than fixed to scheduled times, satisfying crop water requirements more efficiently) belongs to the later work by the citing authors, not to this study. What the study shows is predicted energy savings (up to 36.4%, Table 8; 29,484 kWh/year for scenario 9, Table 9) with minimum hydrant pressure guaranteed.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is an energy-optimisation case study (GA + calibrated hydraulic model) for one small WUA; it contains no measurements or model outputs on crop water use, water conservation or water-application efficiency, so neither water-conservation claim is supported by the study's own results. Authors note difficulty extrapolating to other schemes (Section 3.3).
